correctness.rationale: There are at most two forbidden common neighbors for a same-side pair, so it has distance two; for an omitted cross edge, first choose another right vertex adjacent to its left endpoint, then another left vertex adjacent to both right vertices, giving distance three. Nonempty sets distinguish opposite parts by parity. For two unselected vertices on the same side, the only landmark that can distinguish them is a selected deleted partner of either; thus the undistinguished class consists of the k empty-pair ends plus the unselected unmatched vertices on that side. This proves both inequalities and they exclude the empty set under a,b>=3. Split the generating function at k=0 and k=1. In the latter case all unmatched vertices and all nonempty pair singletons are essential, while any doubleton is reducible; in the former case omit exactly one unmatched vertex on each nonempty unmatched side, which makes every pair singleton essential except when both unmatched sides are empty. This gives the three minimal polynomials, the exact gap condition, and includes t=0. For a crown the empty-pair count is Binomial(n,(1-s)^2), so the asserted limit is its mass at zero and one in the Poisson limit. Independently used Floyd–Warshall and full subset comparison for seven examples covering zero, partial, saturated unequal, and crown deletions; e.g. (4,4,2) has 87 resolving sets with 16 minimal of size 4 and 4 of size 5.
